messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P-2147 fired for host: gpu-host-423 (metric: node_exporter_softlock_count > 0) :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Alert details: kernel softlockup detected, kubelet Unhealthy, host not responding to health probes. Auto-page policy: current on-call -> escalate after 5m if unack'd. Link: https://pagerduty.example/P-2147

mike: acked the page. I'm on it.

sara: thx. grabbing serial and logs. any immediate customer impact?

mike: console shows repeated watchdog resets. some pods in node gpu-pool-2 show CrashLoopBackOff. Not seeing eviction yet but kubelet is flapping.

jin: tagging infra-runbook to check known softlock playbooks @ops-runbook-bot

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook matched: "gpu-host-softlock". Suggested steps: 1) cordon node 2) drain non-critical pods 3) attempt graceful kubelet restart 4) if unresponsive, request power-cycle via IPMI.

mike: cordoning now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-host-423
NODE "gpu-host-423" cordoned
```

sara: starting drain of best-effort pods, skipping daemonsets: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-host-423 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

mike: drain hung on a sidecar that refuses termination. I'm going to evict with force.

jin: FYI I've opened a quick check with telemetry: historically softlocks on this rack linked to BIOS version mismatch after recent maintenance. tagging hw-team.

mike: tried restarting kubelet systemd unit via ssh, no response. ssh still up but kubeletctl shows no heartbeat.

sara: ssh -> sudo systemctl status kubelet: 
```
● kubelet.service - kubelet: Active: activating (start) since 10s; watchdog triggered
... logs showing: "softlockup: CPU stuck for 22s" repeated
```

mike: decision: request IPMI power-cycle. Initiating RMM -> power-cycle request. pinging hw on-call.

oncall-rotation: hw-oncall-1 paged, acknowledging. ETA to rack ~15m.

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: mark node as "maintenance" in inventory and note customer-impact.

sara: quick customer impact check: seeing increased latency for jobs pinned to gpu-pool-2. No full failures yet, but 3 customers running long jobs affected (ids: cust-101, cust-412, cust-990). Notifying support for potential customer outreach.

mike: IPMI returned success, host is powering off. waiting for POST.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed (acknowledged). Logging P-2147 -> incident tracking ticket INC-2025 created.

sara: host back online, BIOS POST ok but kernel shows oops on boot referencing nvidia oom. reapplying kubelet config and starting kubelet.

mike: kubelet came up, started rejoining cluster. re-running drain completion checks.

sara: drained earlier force-evicted pods are now rescheduled. verifying workloads for error spikes.

jin: quick postmortem notes: pre-existing driver build on host was 470.x while fleet standard is 525.x. escalate to hw-team to schedule rolling driver updates for rack.

mike: tagging oncall handoff: I'll finish stabilization, @sara please take primary for monitoring and customer comms for remainder of shift.

sara: ack. will watch telemetry for 30m and confirm no regressions then sign off. posting summary to incidents channel after stabilization. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for on-call. P-2147 -> resolved by power-cycle. Follow-ups: driver alignment, add node softlock probe to early-detection alerts, update runbook to include forced-evict timeout tuning.

mike: adding quick commands used to notes: 
```
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-host-423
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.20.30.3 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle
```

sara: creating support ticket for customers flagged and drafting outreach. cc: support-leads.

jin: logging a follow-up ticket for infra: INFRA-789 (driver drift in rack-7).

mike: thanks all. handoff complete.

sara: end of thread.
